title: An acyclic dg hull preserves monomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra. Use left sheaf dg modules and signed shifts as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Let $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$ be the category of integer-graded left $\mathcal A$-module sheaves, with no differential and with degree-zero module maps. Let $F$ forget the differential from sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-modules to $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$. There is a functor $G$ in the reverse direction and natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{dg}}(G(N),M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)}(N,F(M))$. For every graded module sheaf $N$, every underlying cohomology sheaf of $G(N)$ is zero. For every monomorphism $N\hookrightarrow N^{\prime}$ of graded module sheaves, the induced dg map $G(N)\to G(N^{\prime})$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); preservation of monomorphisms follows from the natural unit and cokernel descriptions in 0FSL, as used in 0FSS. Left modules by the graded opposite algebra.

proof.text: Work in the fixed universes. For a graded left module sheaf $N$, set $G(N)^n=N^n\oplus N^{n-1}$ as an $\mathcal O$-module sheaf: on an open $V$ its sections are pairs $(x,y)$ with $x\in N^n(V)$ and $y\in N^{n-1}(V)$, with componentwise restrictions. The sheaf gluing and uniqueness conditions hold separately in the two coordinates. Define $D(x,y)=(0,x)$ in degree $n+1$; this is a sheaf map and $D^2=0$. No product indexed by all degrees is needed: each degree uses just two sheaves.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: For a homogeneous local section $a\in\mathcal A^p$, define $a\cdot(x,y)=(ax-(-1)^p d_{\mathcal A}(a)y,\,(-1)^p ay)$. The terms have degrees $p+n$ and $p+n-1$; the formula is $\mathcal O$-bilinear, additive and compatible with restriction. It is unital since $d_{\mathcal A}(1)=0$ (the derivation identity gives $d(1)=d(1)+d(1)$). For $b\in\mathcal A^q$, expanding $a\cdot(b\cdot(x,y))$ gives $(abx-(-1)^q a\,d(b)y-(-1)^{p+q}d(a)by,\,(-1)^{p+q}aby)$. This equals $(ab)\cdot(x,y)$ because $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^p a\,d(b)$. Thus the displayed action is associative.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: The dg module identity is a direct computation: $D(a\cdot(x,y))=(0,ax-(-1)^p d(a)y)$, while $d(a)\cdot(x,y)+(-1)^p a\cdot D(x,y)$ has first coordinate $d(a)x-d(a)x=0$ (using $d^2(a)=0$), and second coordinate $(-1)^{p+1}d(a)y+ax$. Hence these expressions agree. This makes $G(N)$ a left sheaf dg module with the conventions of the statement. For a degree-zero graded $\mathcal A$-linear map $u:N\to N'$, put $G(u)(x,y)=(u(x),u(y))$. This commutes with $D$ and the action formula since $u(ax)=a u(x)$ and $u(d(a)y)=d(a)u(y)$. Componentwise composition and identities show that $G$ is a functor.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: Given a degree-zero graded $\mathcal A$-linear sheaf map $f:N\to F(M)$, define $\widetilde f:G(N)\to M$ by $\widetilde f(x,y)=f(x)+d_Mf(y)$. This has degree zero and commutes with restrictions. It is a chain map since $d_M\widetilde f(x,y)=d_Mf(x)=\widetilde f(0,x)$. It is $\mathcal A$-linear: for $a$ of degree $p$, expanding $\widetilde f(a\cdot(x,y))$ gives $a f(x)-(-1)^p d(a)f(y)+(-1)^p d_M(a f(y))=a f(x)+a d_Mf(y)$ by the dg Leibniz identity. Thus $\widetilde f$ is a dg module morphism.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: Conversely, for a dg map $t:G(N)\to M$, define $f(x)=t(x,0)$. The inclusion $x\mapsto(x,0)$ is graded $\mathcal A$-linear by the action formula, so $f$ is graded $\mathcal A$-linear. Since $(x,y)=(x,0)+D(y,0)$, the chain-map identity forces $t(x,y)=f(x)+d_M f(y)$. The two assignments are inverse, because $\widetilde f(x,0)=f(x)$. They are natural: for $u:N'\to N$, $\widetilde{f u}=\widetilde f\,G(u)$ by evaluation on $(x,y)$; for a dg map $v:M\to M'$, $\widetilde{v f}=v\widetilde f$ since $v d_M=d_{M'}v$. Inverting these natural bijections gives exactly $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{dg}}(G(N),M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)}(N,F(M))$.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: In degree $n$, the kernel sheaf of $D:G(N)^n\to G(N)^{n+1}$ consists precisely of pairs $(0,y)$. It is also the image of $D:G(N)^{n-1}\to G(N)^n$, since $D(y,0)=(0,y)$. These identities are identities of sheaf maps: the projection $(x,y)\mapsto y$ restricts to an inverse from the kernel onto $N^{n-1}$, and $y\mapsto(y,0)$ gives the required lift in degree $n-1$. Consequently the kernel and image subsheaves coincide, so their quotient, the $n$th underlying cohomology sheaf, is zero. This holds for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: Let $u:N\to N'$ be a categorical monomorphism of graded module sheaves. To justify using injectivity on sections, define $K^n(V)=\{x\in N^n(V):u(x)=0\}$. These form sheaves by gluing in $N^n$ and checking $u(x)=0$ locally. They are stable under the graded $\mathcal A$-action since $u(ax)=a u(x)$, so they form a graded module sheaf $K$. Its inclusion $j:K\to N$ satisfies $u j=0=u\,0$. Cancellation by the monomorphism $u$ gives $j=0$. On each open and in each degree $j$ is the inclusion of the displayed subset, hence that subset is zero. Thus every map $u^n(V)$ is injective. This proves the needed direction directly, without invoking any theorem that forgetful functors preserve monomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0FSK (lemma-dg-hull) and 0FSL (lemma-dg-hull-acyclic); explicit left-module construction and elementary verification by Q52

proof.text: By construction $G(u)^n(V)$ sends $(x,y)$ to $(u^n(V)x,u^{n-1}(V)y)$, so it is injective by the previous step. If two dg module maps $r,s:P\to G(N)$ satisfy $G(u)r=G(u)s$, this sectionwise injectivity gives $r^n(V)=s^n(V)$ on every open and in every degree. Equality of these components is equality of dg module maps. Hence $r=s$, proving that $G(u)$ is a monomorphism, as required.
